title.narrative: NULL - Indonesia (01-Jan-2016-31-Dec-2017)

description.narrative: Indonesia had been ranking third in the world for the highest Tuberculosis (TB) burden for many years, but very recently (WHO update to Global Report 2009) the country has moved to fifth rank which can be considered as a major achievement of the Program. Out of existing 482 districts in Indonesia, 138 are officially recognized by the government as underserved districts, mostly in remote areas. These districts have been designated as priority areas for accelerated development. The goal of the Program is to decrease morbidity/mortality caused by tuberculosis and to interrupt the chain of transmission of tuberculosis so that it is no longer a public health problem. Among those targeted by the Program will be children, women, people living with HIV, prisoners and community groups. This Program is a consolidation of Round 10 and Round 8 TB grants.
